name: BME280
title: Combined digital humidity, barometric pressure and temperature sensor, I²C and SPI, 2.5 × 2.5 mm metal-lid LGA
summary: A single package holding three sensing elements: relative humidity, absolute barometric pressure and temperature, each read by a shared ADC and delivered as raw codes that the host turns into physical units with factory calibration words stored on the chip. The core runs from 1.71 V to 3.6 V and the interface rail from 1.2 V to 3.6 V; the host talks to it over I²C up to 3.4 MHz or SPI (3- or 4-wire) up to 10 MHz. Sleep, forced (one conversion on request) and normal (free-running with a programmed idle time) modes, per-channel oversampling and an IIR filter on pressure and temperature trade current against noise; at one reading per second with all three channels it draws 3.6 µA. Registers and pressure/temperature behaviour match the BMP280.

pins.function: Ground; tie to the board ground in every interface mode.

pins.name: CSB
pins.function: Chip select, low active, with an internal pull-up of 70 kΩ to 190 kΩ to VDDIO. Wire straight to VDDIO for I²C; drive it from the host as chip select for 3- or 4-wire SPI. A low level on it at any time after reset locks the part in SPI until the next power-on reset.

pins.name: SDI
pins.function: SPI 4-wire data in; SPI 3-wire data in and out; I²C SDA (open drain to ground, needs an external pull-up to VDDIO).

pins.name: SCK
pins.function: Serial clock: SPI SCK, or I²C SCL. High-impedance input; the part never stretches the clock.

pins.name: SDO
pins.function: SPI 4-wire data out. In I²C it sets bit 0 of the address: ground gives 0x76, VDDIO gives 0x77; it must not float. Do not connect in 3-wire SPI, where it is high impedance.

circuits.title: I²C connection
circuits.description: The sensor on an I²C bus. CSB goes straight to VDDIO, which selects I²C at power-up. R1 and R2 pull SDA and SCL up to VDDIO; 4.7 kΩ is a usual value, chosen in practice from bus load and timing. SDO sets address bit 0: ground for 0x76, VDDIO for 0x77. C1 decouples VDD and C2 decouples VDDIO, 100 nF each.

operation.text: VDD feeds every internal analog and digital block; VDDIO feeds only the interface pads. The POR circuit clears the logic and registers once both rails reach their minimum; the rails may rise in any order and at any rate, and the part then waits in sleep mode. With VDDIO present and VDD absent the interface pins stay high impedance, so the bus can run before the sensor core is powered. A reset comes from cycling VDD or writing 0xB6 to the reset register; cycling VDDIO alone does not reset.
No interface pin (SDI, SDO, SCK, CSB) may sit at a logic high while VDDIO is off: current through the ESD diodes can destroy the part.

mode[1:0] picks one of three modes. Sleep: nothing is measured, every register can be read and written, current is lowest; the part enters it after reset. Forced: one measurement cycle runs with the current settings, results land in the data registers and the part drops back to sleep; each new reading needs forced mode written again, which suits slow sampling or host-timed reads. Normal: the part loops between a measurement cycle and an idle period set by t_sb (0.5 ms to 1000 ms), and the latest result is always readable without further writes; standby current is a little above sleep current. Normal mode is the one to pair with the IIR filter.

From power-off the part goes to sleep once both rails are up. Sleep moves to forced (mode 01) or normal (mode 11); normal returns to sleep with mode 00; forced returns to sleep on its own. A mode command written during a measurement waits until that measurement ends, and further mode commands or writes to ctrl_hum are ignored until it takes effect. Other transitions are tested for stability but are not a recommended use.

Each cycle measures temperature, then pressure, then humidity, each with its own oversampling and each skippable by setting its osrs field to 0; a skipped output reads 0x80000 (pressure, temperature) or 0x8000 (humidity). With the IIR filter on, the first result after a filter reset is copied straight into the filter memory; later results update it, and the filter memory goes to the output registers. Skipping temperature allows faster pressure readings.

The filter smooths short pressure disturbances such as a door slamming or wind across the port, lowers the bandwidth of the pressure and temperature outputs and raises their resolution to 20 bits. A larger coefficient slows the response, measured in samples, so the response time depends on the output data rate. Writing the filter field resets it. A channel that is skipped keeps its filter memory unchanged, and when re-enabled it continues from that old memory unless the filter is rewritten. Sampling is not continuous, so disturbances faster than the sample rate alias; pressure changes from windows opening and closing are below 5 Hz, which a 10 Hz output rate covers.

The noise tables give the mean standard deviation of 32 consecutive readings at the fastest sampling, taken in a controlled setting so that slow drift is excluded. Humidity and pressure noise depend on temperature oversampling too, since the temperature value enters their compensation; the listed combinations give the best ratio of noise to power.

Read the data in one burst: 0xF7 to 0xFC for pressure and temperature, or 0xF7 to 0xFE to add humidity. Pressure and temperature are unsigned 20-bit, humidity unsigned 16-bit. In normal mode a conversion can finish mid-read; the new results then wait in shadow registers and are moved into the data registers when the burst ends (CSB rising in SPI, a stop condition in I²C), so a single burst always returns one consistent set. Separate reads can mix data from different cycles. Under I²C, reading straight through the unused pressure bytes is quicker than two separate reads.

The raw codes become °C, Pa and %RH only through the compensation formulas and the calibration words dig_T1…dig_T3, dig_P1…dig_P9 and dig_H1…dig_H6 stored in the chip's NVM. Temperature is computed first: its t_fine value feeds the pressure and humidity formulas. Bosch Sensortec supplies an API for readout and compensation and recommends it. Integer forms exist for 32-bit and 64-bit arithmetic, a reduced-accuracy all-32-bit pressure form for 8-bit controllers, and a double-precision form for PC tools.

Registers are 8 bits wide. A change to ctrl_hum takes effect only when ctrl_meas is written afterwards. A config write can be dropped while in normal mode but is always accepted in sleep mode. Reserved registers must not be written. Every conversion begins by copying the NVM calibration image again (status bit im_update).

Pressure and temperature control and readout follow the BMP280 register for register. The differences: chip ID 0x60 instead of 0x56/0x57/0x58; t_sb codes 110 and 111 mean 10 ms and 20 ms instead of 2000 ms and 4000 ms; and with the filter on, pressure and temperature are always 20 bits. The BME280 at SDO high answers on the BMP280's I²C address, 0x77.

CSB high at power-up selects I²C; CSB pulled low selects SPI, and from the first low level on CSB, clocked or not, I²C stays off until the next power-on reset, so SPI traffic to other devices is never taken as I²C. Because start-up waits for both rails, the power-up sequence cannot mis-select. If CSB comes from a host pin instead of VDDIO in an I²C design, that pin must already be at the VDDIO level during the sensor's power-on reset, or the part stays in SPI.

A slave compatible with I²C specification 2.1 in standard, fast and high-speed modes. The 7-bit address is 111011x: SDO low gives 0x76, SDO at VDDIO gives 0x77, and SDO may change while running but must not float. Neither bus pad is a true open drain: both carry ESD diodes to VDDIO and to GND. SCL is a high-impedance input because the part never stretches the clock. SDA drives low only and needs an external pull-up to VDDIO. A write sends the address with RW = 0 followed by register-address/data pairs and a stop. A read first writes the register address, then a stop or repeated start, then the address with RW = 1; data come from auto-incremented addresses until the master answers NACK and stops.

Modes 00 and 11 are both accepted; the level of SCK when CSB falls tells which. 4-wire uses CSB, SCK, SDI in and SDO out; setting spi3w_en makes it 3-wire, with SDI carrying data both ways and SDO high impedance. CSB is low active with an internal pull-up. Data on SDI are latched on the rising SCK edge and SDO changes on the falling edge; SCK must stay steady while CSB changes. Only seven address bits are sent: bit 7 of the control byte is RW (0 write, 1 read). Writes are control/data pairs repeated inside one CSB low period; a read sends one control byte and then streams auto-incremented registers out of SDO (SDI in 3-wire).
Both interfaces do single-byte writes, multi-byte writes as address/data pairs, single-byte reads, and multi-byte reads from one start address that increments automatically.

Leave at least 0.1 mm above the metal lid. Give the housing a vent if the outside air pressure is to be measured. Keep liquids off the part. The die is light-sensitive while operating (photocurrent in silicon); the vent position limits exposure, and strong light on the sensor should be avoided. Vapour-phase soldering damages the sensor. Solder height after reflow is at least 50 µm, which decouples the sensor mechanically from the board; the solder drift row assumes it.

Moisture sensitivity level 1 to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020C, handled to J-STD-033A, and rated for lead-free reflow with a 260 °C peak. Exposure outside the humidity operating range, reflow included, can leave an offset in the humidity reading; one of the reconditioning procedures is required to restore calibration.

The self-test routine for the API soft-resets the part, checks the chip ID and the range of the calibration words, then measures temperature and pressure and compares them with adjustable plausibility limits (default 0 to 40 °C and 900 to 1100 hPa). Readings stuck at the ADC end-stops point to a broken bond wire or sensing element; some faults do not clip and are caught only by the plausibility limits. It waits 9 ms in all (2 ms after the soft reset, 7 ms for the conversion), issues 4 writes and 6 reads (4 bytes out, 34 bytes in), and the bus time with burst reads is about 6.0 ms at 100 kHz I²C, 1.5 ms at 400 kHz I²C or 0.5 ms at 1 MHz SPI; the whole run takes 10.5 ms at 400 kHz I²C. The soft reset may be left out on a part known to be fresh from power-up. Only the read path is proven by the communication check.

Meets RoHS directive 2011/65/EU with amendment 2015/863/EU, and is halogen-free. The package may come from more than one qualified source; the technical parameters are identical, while chemical content and internal structure can differ.
